niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces that feel polished, structured, and complete, with clear hierarchy, strong sectioning, and realistic information coverage. They often favor lighter, calmer surfaces and integrated low-contrast cards, but their stronger pattern is less about one fixed style and more about UIs that feel intentional, legible, and compositionally resolved. They respond well to complete settings/list layouts, clear grouping, balanced spacing, and concise, decisive messaging. They also repeatedly prefer context-rich screens over sparse or isolated presentations, and tend to like restrained, cohesive visual systems over noisy or fragmented ones.

criteria.description: Clear sectioning, bold or well-defined headers, labeled groups, and an easy-to-scan hierarchy with strong separation between content areas.
Layouts that feel fully populated, realistic, and complete, with enough visible options, rows, or contextual details to seem genuinely usable rather than sparse or placeholder-like.
Modular, orderly composition where cards, rows, or sections are grouped coherently and do not compete in the same flow; prefers layouts that feel organized rather than fragmented or mixed together.
Sharper, more defined, more polished interfaces with resolved rows, cleaner typography, stronger visual finish, and no unfinished or awkward elements.
Enough open spacing and vertical rhythm to keep the interface calm and scannable, avoiding cramped stacking or crowded flows.
A cohesive, controlled visual language with integrated components, muted or refined accents, and less decorative clutter, avoiding noisy, overly promotional, or visually fragmented treatments.
Copy and presentation that are concrete, matter-of-fact, and context-rich, with explicit status details or action framing rather than vague, generic, or overly reassuring wording.
